_note: Draft written from general knowledge for the analyst's get_species_profile tool. The Product lead should check it before the demo.

eurasian_collared_dove.habitat: Towns, suburbs and farmland with scattered trees
eurasian_collared_dove.diet: Seeds and grain, often at bird feeders, livestock yards and grain elevators
eurasian_collared_dove.migration: Non-migratory. Spreads by young birds dispersing, often north and west
eurasian_collared_dove.nesting: Platform nests in trees and on buildings; several broods a year
knownThreats: None major; it is an introduced species in North America
eurasian_collared_dove.notes: Introduced to the Bahamas in the 1970s, reached Florida in the 1980s and spread across most of the US since.

chimney_swift.habitat: Towns and cities; feeds high in open sky
chimney_swift.diet: Flying insects caught on the wing
chimney_swift.migration: Long-distance migrant; winters in the upper Amazon basin of South America
chimney_swift.nesting: Nests and roosts in chimneys, formerly in hollow trees
knownThreats: Loss of open chimneys that are capped or demolished
Fewer flying insects, including from pesticides
chimney_swift.notes: Listed as Vulnerable by the IUCN after long declines.

western_meadowlark.diet: Insects such as grasshoppers and beetles in summer; seeds in winter
western_meadowlark.migration: Short-distance; northern birds move south for the winter
knownThreats: Early hay mowing that destroys nests
western_meadowlark.notes: State bird of Nebraska and five other states.

eastern_meadowlark.habitat: Grasslands, hayfields and pastures in the east
eastern_meadowlark.diet: Insects in summer; seeds in winter
eastern_meadowlark.migration: Short-distance; northern birds move south for the winter
knownThreats: Loss of grassland to development and to forest regrowth on old farms
Early hay mowing that destroys nests
eastern_meadowlark.notes: Listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN.

wood_thrush.habitat: Mature deciduous and mixed forest with a shrub layer
wood_thrush.diet: Insects and other invertebrates from leaf litter; fruit in late summer
wood_thrush.migration: Long-distance migrant; winters in Central America
wood_thrush.nesting: Cup nest in a shrub or small tree
knownThreats: Forest broken into small patches, which raises nest predation and cowbird parasitism
Loss of wintering forest in Central America
wood_thrush.notes: Listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN.

bald_eagle.habitat: Near large lakes, rivers and coasts with tall trees
bald_eagle.diet: Mostly fish; also waterbirds and carrion
bald_eagle.migration: Partial migrant; northern birds move to open water in winter
bald_eagle.nesting: Very large stick nest in a tall tree, reused for years
knownThreats: Lead poisoning from ammunition and fishing tackle
Collisions with vehicles and power lines
bald_eagle.notes: Recovered after the 1972 US ban on DDT and legal protection; removed from the endangered species list in 2007.

carolina_wren.habitat: Dense undergrowth in woods, thickets and suburban gardens
carolina_wren.nesting: Nests in cavities and nooks, including in buildings
knownThreats: Severe winters, which cause large die-offs at the northern edge of its range
carolina_wren.notes: Its range has moved north, linked to milder winters and bird feeders.

black_vulture.habitat: Open country and forest edges, often near roads and towns
black_vulture.nesting: Lays eggs on the ground in caves, hollow logs or abandoned buildings
black_vulture.notes: Its range has expanded north over recent decades.
